title: Zero-FI Regular ADHM Data and Framed ASD Connections

items.title: Donaldson's ADHM matrix equations in the source convention
items.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. Write $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. The Donaldson source convention for these four matrices is

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

The second equality is an equality of Hermitian endomorphisms of $V$. It is an algebraic convention from the displayed source equations; it does not by itself assert the full-rank condition on the source's ADHM linear map or an identification with the run's raw moment maps.

items.statement: Assume AC. Let $E$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle on a finite-dimensional complex manifold, and let $D''$ be a smooth complex-linear operator from its smooth sections to smooth $E$-valued $(0,1)$-forms satisfying $D''(fs)=\bar\partial f\otimes s+fD''s$. Extend it to bundle-valued forms by the graded Leibniz rule and suppose $(D'')^2=0$. Near every point there is a smooth invertible frame matrix $G$ with $D''G=0$. The changes between these frames are holomorphic, defining a unique holomorphic vector-bundle structure with Dolbeault operator $D''$. A smooth bundle map intertwines two such operators exactly when it is holomorphic for these structures. The construction is local and requires no projective GAGA, coherence or global vanishing theorem.

items.title: Entrywise conjugation does not match the raw ADHM real moment map
items.statement:
Let $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,P,Q)$ obey the source equations stated in the following references section. Under the proposed substitution

$$B_i=\overline{\alpha_i},\qquad I=\overline P,\qquad J=\overline Q,$$

the raw complex moment map vanishes, but the raw real moment map is

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y,$$

where $C=[\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]$, $X=PP^\dagger$, and $Y=Q^\dagger Q$. The conjugated source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so on source solutions the proposed raw real moment map equals $2\overline C$; the source equations alone therefore do not establish its vanishing. This failure occurs for the explicit $k=N=2$ source solution in the proof below.

items.title: Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data
items.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

items.title: Determinant flatness and charge normalization for framed U(N) ASD data
items.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

items.title: Smooth framed bundle of sections over real twistor lines
items.statement:
Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let
$$\mathscr L=\{(g,z)\in G\times Z:z\in g\},\qquad p(g,z)=g,\qquad e(g,z)=z$$
be the universal line family and its projections. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with the positive Ward reality datum from the preceding “Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data” definition: a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$, linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second, satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $\sigma$ is the fixed antiholomorphic involution on $Z$. For each real line $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$, where $\pi:Z\to S^4$ is the twistor projection fixed in that definition, the pairing defines $h_x(s,t)=b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ on $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, independent of $z\in L_x$; assume $h_x$ is positive definite and $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is holomorphically trivial. Equip its fibers with the metric transported from $h_x$ by evaluation, as in that definition. Let $L_\infty=\pi^{-1}(\infty)$ and fix a unitary trivialization $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{L_\infty}^{\oplus N}$ for this metric. Write $p^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $e^{\mathrm{an}}$ for the induced analytic maps. Identify $S^4$ with its real-line locus in $G$, write $g_x\in G$ for the line parameter corresponding to $x\in S^4$, and put $\mathcal H=(p^{\mathrm{an}})_*(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$.

Let $\operatorname{ev}:(p^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal H\to(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$ be the canonical evaluation morphism, which evaluates a family of holomorphic sections at the point of its line.

Then, for every real line $L_x$, the canonical degree-zero analytic base-change map
$$\beta^0_{g_x}:\mathcal H_{g_x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}}\mathbb C(g_x)\longrightarrow H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$$
is an isomorphism, where $\mathbb C(g_x)=\mathcal O_{G^{\mathrm{an}},g_x}/\mathfrak m_{g_x}\cong\mathbb C$ is the residue field. The restriction $\mathcal H|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with fibre $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ at $x$, and evaluation identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $(e^{\mathrm{an}})^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

items.title: Conditional framed Penrose–Ward correspondence on the round four-sphere
items.statement:
Assume full AC and the exact projective GAGA comparison used below. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ defined above. On the Ward side take a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum, and a unitary framing on $L_\infty$. Require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line, and require $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$. Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For each section of $\widehat E_x$, extend it holomorphically and uniquely to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of $L_x$ and differentiate this extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by the positive holomorphic reality pairing is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between based unitary gauge classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward bundles. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is the connection on the planes $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and compact torus action. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

items.title: Chern character and charge of the normalized twistor monad
items.statement:
Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the cohomology of a linear monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the twistor orientation specified in the Definition, if $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfies $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$, then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

items.title: Conditional Penrose vanishing from positive scalar curvature
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. Suppose the following conditional Penrose-transform input is supplied for both $\mathcal E$ and its dual $\mathcal E^\vee$: there are injective linear maps

$$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/6)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

items.title: Conditional twistor vanishing and normalized monad reconstruction
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Use the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing input stated below for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

items.title: Real monad normalization, regularity, framing and charge
items.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let a framed real Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ have the normalized linear monad with vector-space dimensions $k,2k+N,k$. Then the real monad is equivalent to a raw datum $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ on $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ in exactly the convention

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$

The tuple is regular exactly when the associated quaternionic construction is pointwise nondegenerate. Its kernel projection connection extends over $\infty$, has the specified framing, and equals the Ward connection. Changes of normalized monad bases induce exactly the $U(k)$ action on raw data, and inverse matrix extraction recovers the same $U(k)$ orbit. The resulting charge is $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. The entrywise conjugation candidate is refuted by the recorded comparison lemma and is not used in the intrinsic real monad normalization.

items.title: Conditional zero-FI regular ADHM and framed ASD correspondence
items.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}$ be the quotient by $U(k)$ of the raw data satisfying both zero moment equations and stable-and-costable regularity in the conventions stated in the following references section. Let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ with $q_N=-k$ in those same conventions. Conditional on the real monad normalization and Ward inputs stated below, the construction gives a $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$-equivariant bijection

$$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}\;\longleftrightarrow\;\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}.$$

The zero-FI real quotient is also diffeomorphic to the stable-and-costable complex $GL(k)$ quotient. Under the stated projective GAGA and family base-change hypotheses, the corresponding framed sheaves on $\mathbb P^2$ are exactly the locally free locus among the framed torsion-free sheaves with rank $N$ and Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$. The positive-FI stable quotient includes non-locally-free sheaves and is not identified with the ordinary framed ASD moduli. Under the same family and normal-form hypotheses, the correspondence is compatible with first-order framed deformations and their tangent spaces.

items.title: Rank-one regular zero-FI ADHM and ordinary ASD boundary
items.statement:
Assume AC and the exact rank-two regular zero-FI ADHM/ASD correspondence, with all its actual analytic and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites. Fix $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,1}$ be the orbit set by $U(V)$ of $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ with

$$[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad [B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0,$$

such that words in the $B_i$ applied to $I(W)$ span $V$ and no nonzero common invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$. On the positively stereographically oriented unit round $S^4$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,1}$ be the set of smooth Hermitian line bundles $L$, smooth unitary connections $A$ with $F_A^+=0$, and unitary framings $\Phi:L_\infty\to\mathbb C$, with $q_1=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int F_A\wedge F_A=-k$, modulo framed unitary isomorphisms. After a fixed framed bundle is chosen, its gauge group consists of smooth unitary automorphisms equal to identity at infinity.

The regular complex $GL(V)$ quotient, defined by retaining the complex equation and the same stability and costability, has the same empty-or-point classification under the zero-FI real/complex quotient identification. For $k>0$ both ordinary sets are empty. For $k=0$ they are the single empty raw datum and the framed flat line, respectively, with no framed stabilizer. This identification is equivariant for $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$, with $h=e^{-1}$, raw action $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$ and connection action by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing with $h$; on the resulting point these actions are trivial.

A first-order real Hermitian family here is over $D=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ with involution $\varepsilon^\dagger=\varepsilon$. On the raw side use free $D$-modules of ranks $k,1$, the displayed equations over $D$, regular reduction, fixed framing module, and unitary $D$-linear changes of basis. On the connection side use locally free smooth Hermitian line-bundle deformations with framed special fiber and a unitary connection $A_0+\varepsilon a$, satisfying ASD coefficientwise, modulo unitary gauge transformations with framed reduction and value identity at infinity. For $k>0$ these groupoids are empty; for $k=0$ each is equivalent to the one-object groupoid with trivial automorphism group. The identification commutes with reduction, infinitesimal scalar base changes preserving the involution, and the compact action. In particular it identifies their zero tangent spaces and restricts to the exact locally-free/base-change family range in the rank-two correspondence. No positive-FI quotient, its non-locally-free rank-one boundary, or its fixed-point series is identified with ordinary ASD moduli.

items.title: The zero-charge regular datum and framed flat ASD sector
items.statement: For every $N\geq2$, the $k=0$ regular zero-FI ADHM quotient consists of the unique empty datum, and the framed ASD sector with $q_N=0$ consists of the framed flat connection on the trivial rank-$N$ bundle; the framing removes its based-gauge stabilizer.

items.title: A positive-FI point with a non-locally-free framed sheaf
items.statement:
Take $N=k=1$ and $\zeta>0$. The datum $B_1=B_2=0$, $I=\sqrt\zeta$, $J=0$ is a stable positive-FI solution but is not costable and does not lie in the zero-FI regular locus. Its stable complex orbit has the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad

$$\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}\mathcal O^{\oplus3}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,z_0)}\mathcal O(1),$$

whose middle cohomology is the ideal sheaf of $p=[1:0:0]$; it is torsion-free and not locally free at $p$. Thus this positive-FI point lies on the non-locally-free boundary excluded from the ordinary zero-FI framed ASD correspondence.
